In [[mathematics]], '''Waraszkiewicz spirals''' are subsets of the [[Plane (geometry)|plane]] introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Waraszkiewicz|year=1932|authorlink=Zenon Waraszkiewicz}}. Waraszkiewicz spirals give an example of an uncountable family of pairwise incomparable continua, meaning that there is no [[Continuous map (topology)|continuous map]] from one onto another.
